# Simple OLS

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

source("R/run_simple_ols.R")

res <- run_simple_ols()
fig_path  <- res$figpath
table_out <- res$table

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  comment = "",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
### Learning objectives
- Understand the assumptions underlying the linear regression model
- Interpret OLS coefficients in economic terms
- Distinguish between statistical and economic significance
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Key takeaways
- Ordinary Least Squares provides unbiased estimates under standard assumptions
- Coefficients measure marginal effects ceteris paribus
- Model interpretation depends critically on correct specification
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
### Common pitfalls
- Interpreting correlation as causation
- Ignoring omitted variable bias
- Overemphasizing statistical significance without economic reasoning
:::

## Motivation
Why linear regression remains the workhorse of applied econometrics.

## Model
We consider the standard linear regression model.

## Interpretation
Economic meaning of coefficients and assumptions.

## Empirical example

```{r, fig-ols-fit, fig.cap="OLS fitted line"}
knitr::include_graphics(fig_path)

```{r, tbl-ols}
knitr::kable(
  table_out,
  caption = "OLS coefficient estimates",
  align = "l"
)
```
